title: First-Class Appendices for Print Reports and Zwischenbericht Anhänge
description: Add first-class appendix support to the semio print system (print/tex/): an appendix is a document attached to the main report, behaving like a chapter — numbered A, B, C…, labeled Anhang/Appendix, TOC entry, chip styling, cross-referenceable via \appendixref, listed via \listofappendices. Fix a pre-existing bug where window registers (\listoffigures etc.) render header-only because semio@render@register reads the wrong body macro. Wire the feature into all six print templates (report, paper, flyer n/a, zukunftbau forschungsbericht/zwischenbericht/kompaktbericht). Then apply it to mit-bestand/bericht/zwischenbericht/zwischenbericht.tex: convert 9 Anhang markdown documents from temp/ into 8 LaTeX appendices (A-H), including a 67-project table with per-row avatar images sourced from temp/projekt_bilder/ (downscaled ~600px, copied into zwischenbericht/asset/projekt/). Update body cross-references to use \appendixref. Full plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/print-reports-should-be-joyful-haven.md.
summary:
Fixed the key mismatch the user flagged: the TOC/heading chip for each user story (e.g. "US-S.1.2") and the semantic ID embedded in its title ("US-BB-02", the same ID the Anforderungsmapping table cross-references stories by) shared no relationship at all — "S" was a generic "Stories" placeholder prefix unrelated to the actor-group letters (BB/A/T/E) actually baked into every story's real ID.

Presented four options with real tradeoffs (restructure to match roots / drop the auto-chip and keep only the embedded ID / strip IDs from titles and adopt the auto-number as canonical / just reposition to reduce visual competition) since this affects document structure and cross-referencing, not just a rendering detail. User chose to restructure.

Implemented in anhang/user-stories.tex: replaced the single `\appendixsection[S]{User Stories}` wrapping all four actor-group `\subsection`s with four separate `\appendixsection[BB]{...}`, `[A]{...}`, `[T]{...}`, `[E]{...}` — one per actor group, using the exact letters already embedded in that group's story IDs. Each of the 35 individual stories was promoted from `\paragraph` to `\subsection` (now the direct child level of `\appendixsection`), so their chips became US-BB.1…US-BB.10, US-A.1…US-A.12, US-T.1…US-T.6, US-E.1…US-E.7 — sharing the exact same prefix root as each story's embedded ID (US-BB-01 etc.), rather than an unrelated "US-S.1.2". The remaining dot-vs-hyphen/zero-padding difference (US-BB.2 vs US-BB-02) was an explicit, agreed-on tradeoff of this option, not left unresolved.

Verified: rebuilt the zwischenbericht clean (zero errors, zero duplicate-identifier errors despite adding 4 new sibling prefixes under the same "US" appendix), zero unresolved references, and confirmed via the built PDF that every one of the 35 story chips now shares its title's ID root, the four actor-group chips (US-BB, US-A, US-T, US-E) render correctly as their own TOC entries, and the body's existing cross-references ("Anlage US", "Anlage US-AM") are unaffected.
